P1.strategy: Cooperate with known-good opponents when it raises their combined welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents, who strictly prefer defection. Update beliefs from observed play.

posts.content: As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish opponents. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for incentives and uncertainty.
As a good player, favor C against likely-good opponents; choose D only when evidence makes the opponent likely selfish.
As a good player, favor C against likely good opponents and D against likely selfish ones; update beliefs from observed actions and maximize good players’ total payoff.
Prioritize welfare among good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and use observed actions to adapt.

Cooperate by default: with good opponents, mutual cooperation maximizes good-player total. Defect only when evidence makes opponent likely selfish or predictably defecting; update beliefs from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely good opponents and defect against likely selfish ones; update beliefs from observed actions.
Maximize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against reliably selfish opponents. Track actions and update beliefs; communication is unavailable.
Start cooperative; observe P5’s action and use encounter evidence to update beliefs and future choices.
Defect every round; this maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players, who benefit from exploitation. Use encounter outcomes to update beliefs.
Prioritize mutual cooperation with likely good players; defect when evidence makes selfishness likely. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Against likely-good players, choose C to maximize joint good-player payoff. Selfish players rationally choose D; against a likely-selfish opponent choose D. Update beliefs from observed actions.

As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; selfish players tend to defect. Update beliefs from observed actions, and remember the objective counts only good players’ payoffs.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely-selfish players, especially after observed defection.
Cooperate with good opponents; defect against selfish opponents, who are expected to defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with likely good opponents; defect against likely selfish ones. A selfish player has incentive to defect, so update beliefs from observed defections while allowing for strategic good-player defection.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect when evidence makes an opponent more likely selfish than good.

Cooperate with unknown or likely-good players; defect against players with strong evidence of selfishness, since their payoff is excluded from my objective. Update beliefs from observed actions, while allowing for strategic uncertainty.
Defect each round: it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with players who have cooperated; defect against players who have defected. Update beliefs from observed actions.
P9’s defection suggests selfishness; P6’s cooperation suggests goodness. Against likely-good players, cooperate; defect only when the opponent is more likely selfish than good.
Selfish players strictly prefer D; observed C/C suggests P4 and P7 are good. Cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones, prioritizing total payoffs of good players.
Cooperate with good players to maximize their combined welfare; defect against likely selfish opponents, who benefit us only through mutual defection.
P8 and P10 cooperated; that supports them being good. P9 has no observed evidence, so cooperate by default to maximize good-player welfare; update after the encounter.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good-player welfare; defect against likely selfish players, who always prefer D. Update beliefs cautiously from observed actions.

Against likely-good players, cooperate to protect shared welfare; defect against likely-selfish players to improve good players’ payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions; no messages are available.
Cooperate with P4 absent evidence they are selfish or likely to defect; update beliefs from the encounter, and defect when expected gains to good players favor it.
Defect every round; D yields at least 1 and strictly beats C against either opponent action.
Cooperate when the opponent is likely good; defect when evidence puts their selfishness probability above roughly 1/6. Update beliefs from observed actions, accounting for uncertainty.
As a good player, cooperate with untested opponents unless evidence makes selfishness likely; defect against known defectors to protect good-player welfare.
Against P10, favor C if they seem more likely good than selfish; choose D if evidence makes selfishness more likely. Update beliefs from actions, not claims.

P4, P7, and P10’s mutual cooperation strongly indicates they are good; selfish players should defect. Against P5, cooperate absent evidence of selfishness, since mutual cooperation benefits good players most; defect if evidence suggests P5 is selfish.
Observed C confirms P1, P3, and P8 are good; selfish players strictly prefer D. Cooperate with P6 if good, defect if selfish, to maximize good-player welfare.

Prioritize good-player welfare: cooperate with likely cooperative good opponents; defect when the chance of facing defection or a selfish player makes that better. Update beliefs from observed actions, but treat them as imperfect evidence.

Cooperate with good opponents: mutual C yields 6 good-player points, while unilateral D harms the good partner. Defect against selfish opponents, who have a dominant incentive to D; use observed actions to update cautiously.
Prioritize total welfare of good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents, and defect when evidence suggests they are selfish or will defect. Update beliefs from observed play.

With no evidence about P9, weigh the benefit of mutual cooperation against the risk of facing a selfish defector; update beliefs from our encounter and choose to maximize expected payoffs of good players.
I will defect this round. D strictly dominates C for my payoff against either opponent action.

P5, P6, and P3 are good: selfish players strictly prefer D in a one-shot encounter, so their observed C rules out selfishness. Condition the remaining players’ probabilities on this evidence; against P2, defect if their selfishness probability exceeds 1/6, otherwise cooperate.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with uncertain opponents when mutual cooperation among good players best serves their shared objective; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good-player payoffs; defect when evidence suggests the opponent is selfish.
Cooperate with likely good players to increase good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate to support welfare when facing a likely-good player; adapt to observed actions in later encounters.
Cooperate with no evidence of selfishness: mutual cooperation maximizes good-player total. Update from observed play; defect only when it improves expected payoffs of actual good players.
Cooperate with likely good players to increase total good-player payoffs; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and defect against reliably selfish opponents.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; use encounter evidence to update beliefs and adapt against likely selfish players.
Defect each round; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with unknown opponents while they are more likely good; update beliefs from observed play and defect when evidence favors selfishness.

Cooperate with uncertain opponents when expected good-player welfare favors mutual cooperation; update identity beliefs from observed play and defect when evidence of selfishness makes that better for good players.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents; P9’s defection raises my estimate of their being selfish, but P6 has no direct evidence against them.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to raise good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions as encounters accumulate.
Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good-player welfare; defect when evidence indicates a selfish opponent. P8's cooperation lowers its selfishness probability.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize total good-player payoffs; defect when evidence indicates an opponent is selfish. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate when the expected welfare among good players is higher; use observed actions to update identity beliefs and defect only when that improves good-player welfare.
Cooperate with unknown players to support good players’ combined payoff; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against players with strong evidence of selfishness.
Defect each round; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect only when evidence makes selfishness likely. P6's cooperation indicates they are good, so update beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate when mutual cooperation among good players is likely to improve their total welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect when that better protects good players.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to favor mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate when the opponent may be good: mutual cooperation raises good players’ combined payoff, and cooperating against a defecting good player still benefits them. Defect against known selfish players.
Cooperate when expected good-player welfare favors it; use observed actions to update beliefs and adapt.

Defect against an unobserved opponent when the chance they are selfish makes cooperation costly to good-player welfare. Update beliefs from observed actions; cooperate when that best supports good players.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while defecting only improves our welfare against a selfish defector. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with likely-good opponents to support shared welfare; defect when evidence makes an opponent likely selfish. Update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unknown players to support good players’ combined payoff; observed cooperation makes P1 and P5 good. Adapt if future evidence indicates selfishness.
Defect each round; it strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of the opponent’s action.

Cooperate with likely good opponents to maximize good players’ combined payoff; defect when evidence indicates a selfish opponent. P5 and P6 cooperated, so treat them as good and update remaining probabilities accordingly.
